findings.title: opportunity.account resolves to accounts.account
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM raw.sales_pipeline c LEFT JOIN raw.accounts p ON c.account = p.account WHERE c.account IS NOT NULL AND p.account IS NULL

findings.title: opportunity.sales_agent resolves to sales_teams.sales_agent
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM raw.sales_pipeline c LEFT JOIN raw.sales_teams p ON c.sales_agent = p.sales_agent WHERE c.sales_agent IS NOT NULL AND p.sales_agent IS NULL

findings.title: opportunity.product resolves to products.product
findings.detail: 1,480 rows carry 1 unmapped product label(s): GTXPro. Whitespace-normalised join recovers all of them, so this is a key-hygiene defect, not unknown data.
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM raw.sales_pipeline c LEFT JOIN raw.products p ON c.product = p.product WHERE c.product IS NOT NULL AND p.product IS NULL

findings.title: sales_pipeline.account completeness
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM raw.sales_pipeline WHERE account IS NULL

findings.title: sales_pipeline.engage_date completeness
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM raw.sales_pipeline WHERE engage_date IS NULL

findings.title: sales_pipeline.close_date completeness
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM raw.sales_pipeline WHERE close_date IS NULL

findings.title: sales_pipeline.close_value completeness
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM raw.sales_pipeline WHERE close_value IS NULL

findings.title: close_date/close_value null exactly on open opportunities
findings.detail: 0 open-stage rows wrongly carry a close value; 0 closed-stage rows are missing one. The raw null count on close_date is therefore structural, not a defect - it is the open pipeline and must not be imputed.
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM raw.sales_pipeline WHERE (deal_stage IN ('Prospecting','Engaging') AND (close_date IS NOT NULL OR close_value IS NOT NULL)) OR (deal_stage IN ('Won','Lost') AND (close_date IS NULL OR close_value IS NULL))

findings.title: close_value sign convention by stage
findings.detail: 0 Lost rows with non-zero value; 0 Won rows with value <= 0. Lost opportunities are recorded at 0 rather than null, so revenue aggregations must filter on stage, not on close_value > 0.
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM raw.sales_pipeline WHERE deal_stage='Lost' AND close_value <> 0

findings.title: opportunity_id is unique at the fact grain
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT opportunity_id FROM raw.sales_pipeline GROUP BY opportunity_id HAVING count(*) > 1)

findings.title: accounts.account is unique
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT "account" FROM raw."accounts" GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*)>1)

findings.title: products.product is unique
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT "product" FROM raw."products" GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*)>1)

findings.title: sales_teams.sales_agent is unique
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT "sales_agent" FROM raw."sales_teams" GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*)>1)

findings.title: deal_stage is within the canonical stage list
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM raw.sales_pipeline WHERE deal_stage NOT IN ('Prospecting', 'Engaging', 'Won', 'Lost')

findings.title: accounts.sector spelling conforms to the canonical taxonomy
findings.detail: 1 distinct sector value(s) misspelled: technolgy. Left unrepaired this silently splits the technology segment in every group-by.
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT sector FROM raw.accounts) WHERE sector='technolgy'

findings.title: accounts.office_location spelling conforms to ISO country names
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT office_location FROM raw.accounts) WHERE office_location='Philipines'

findings.title: close_date is never before engage_date
findings.detail: 0 rows with a negative sales cycle
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM raw.sales_pipeline WHERE engage_date IS NOT NULL AND close_date IS NOT NULL AND close_date < engage_date

findings.title: close_date is not in the future
findings.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM raw.sales_pipeline WHERE close_date > current_date
